title: fix(roadmap): check a class claim against the staged source
summary: The design decision claims that `StagedTree` holds the file text of the staged commit, and the class keeps the tracked paths with `ls-files` only. The decision quotes no text of the class, so an implementation step would fail on a text that does not exist.
notes: The plan is the one of the change of #3407 before the class-claim rule of its own check exists: the design decision claims that `StagedTree` holds the file text, and the class holds `ls-files` and no file text.
The change was never merged as this plan, so pull, merge_commit and base_commit hold the issue number and two placeholders: the case reads no commit, and the facts hold the files of its tree.

defects.problem: The design decision says that `StagedTree` holds the file text of the staged commit, and `StagedTree.read` keeps the tracked paths with `ls-files`. The decision quotes no text of the class, so the plan builds on a text that does not exist.
defects.evidence: `src/devops_cli/roadmap/stage/stage_paths.py:143:listing = git(source, "ls-files", "-z", operation=operation)` shows that the tree reader keeps the tracked paths and reads no file text.
defects.message: The plan names `StagedTree` in the design decision and gives no code span that holds text of the class at the staged commit.
